State Bank Of India vs Amar Singh on 10 August, 2026
FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026

DISMISSED PAGE 1 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026

 CORAM:
 HON'BLE JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL
 (PRESIDENT)
 HON'BLE MS. BIMLA KUMARI, MEMBER (FEMALE)
 Present: Mr. R.K. Sinha, counsel for the Appellant appeared through
 VC.
 None for the Respondent.

 PER: HON'BLE JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL,
 PRESIDENT
 JUDGMENT
1. The facts of the case as per the District Commission record are as under:
"...1. The Complainant has stated that he is maintaining
 Account No.10101400411 with the OP since 2002. He is Lab
 Assistant in Government Boys Sr. Sec. School, New Ashok
 Nagar, East Delhi and his salary was credited in the said
 account. On 10.10.2018 he had withdrawn Rs.5000/- from the
 ATM of OP located at Himatpuri, Delhi and there was balance
 of Rs.1,12,472/- on 11.10.2018 a sum of Rs.17,540/- was
 credited in his account and thus there was a balance of
 Rs.1,30,012/- on 11.10.2018.
2. On 22.10.2018 when he went to ATM of the Bank to
 withdraw some amount then he could not withdraw the same
 as there was no sufficient balance in his account. Surprised he
 immediately went to the Branch and got his Pass-book
 updated. Upon updation of his Pass-book he found that on
 12.10.2012 some unknown person had withdrawn Rs.20,000/-
 each 4 times thus totaling Rs.80,000/- by way of ATM. Further
 on the same day i.e. 12.10.2018 a sum of Rs.40,000/- and
 Rs.10,000/- were also transferred from his account to the
 account of one Mr. Sonu. He met the Branch Manager of the
 Bank and submitted letter dated 22.10.2018 with request to
 recover the amount so unauthorizedly withdrawn from his
 account and pay to him. The said letter was acknowledged by
 the OP Bank however no amount was paid to him.
DISMISSED PAGE 2 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026
3. Complainant also lodged FIR No.420 in Police Station,
 Mayur Vihar, Phase-I on 22.10.2018 but no action was taken
 to arrest the accused.
4. On 06.03.2019 he submitted another letter to the OP Bank
 but still there was no response. Complainant thereafter filed
 this Complaint seeking following reliefs:
a. To direct the OP to pay an amount of Rs.1,30,000/-
with prevailing interest of saving account to the
 Complainant;
b. To direct the OP to pay an amount equivalent to
 Rs.10,000/- as cost of this proceedings and advocate
 fee;
c. To direct the OP to pay a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as
 compensation for loss, mental pain and
 inconvenience suffered by the Complainant;
 d. Any other relief which this Forum may grant in
 favour of the Complainant in the interest of justice.
5. The Complainant on 28.08.2019 filed application for
 amendment of complaint which was allowed wherein he has
 added that he received message from OP Bank on 12.10.2018
 but he could not go through the contents and ignored the
 message and got it deleted. Further on 22.10.2018 when he
 met the Branch Manager of OP Bank, he demanded CCTV
 footage of 12.10.2018 of the concerned ATM but the Branch
 Manager refused. The said amendment was allowed on
 29.08.2019."
2. The District Commission after taking into consideration the material available
 on record passed the order dated 21.08.2023, whereby it held as under:
"9. The case of the Complainant is that he is having account
 No. 10101400411 with the OP since 2002. On 10.10.2018 he
 had withdrawn Rs.5000/- from ATM of OP Bank and there was
 a balance of Rs.1,30,012/- on 11.10.2018. Thereafter on
 12.10.2018 there was unauthorized ATM withdrawal 4 times
 of Rs.20,000/- each and another transfer of amount from his

DISMISSED PAGE 3 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026

 account of Rs.40,000/- and Rs.10,000/- on the same day to the
 account of one Mr. Sonu. There was remaining balance of
 Rs.2/-in the account of Complainant on 22.10.2018.
10. The Complainant has stated in his application amending
 the complaint that he had received some message from OP on
 12.10.2018 but he could not go through the contents and
 ignored the message and got it deleted.
11. On 22.10.2018 when he went to withdraw some amount
 from his account through ATM then the same was not
 successful as there was no sufficient balance in his account.
 Immediately Complainant approached OP Bank and got his
 Pass-book updated (Exhibit-CW-1/2) which revealed ATM
 withdrawal of Rs.80,000/-by way of 4 withdrawals of
 Rs.20,000/- each and further Transfer Entry of Rs.40,000/-
 and Rs.10,000/- in his account on 12.10.2018 to the account
 of one Mr. Sonu. On the same day i.e. 12.10.2018 he made
 complaint to OP by way of letter (Exhibit CW-1/3) about it
 which was received by them and sought refund of the amount
 so withdrawn from his account. No action was taken by the OP
 and Complainant wrote another letter which was received by
 the OP Bank on 06.03.2019 again requesting the OP to refund
 the amount to him.
12. The case revolves around the controversy as to how such
 a big amount of Rs.80,000/- got withdrawn by way of ATM in
 the account of the Complainant on single day i.e. 12.10.2018
 and further Rs.40,000/- and Rs.10,000/- was also transferred
 from his account to the account of one Mr. Sonu.
13. In case of receipt of complaint of unauthorized withdrawal
 in any customer's account by way of ATM, the first and the

DISMISSED PAGE 4 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026

 foremost action the concerned Bank is required to take is to
 secure CCTV footage of that day of transaction and
 examine/analyse it to come to the conclusion whether it was
 authorized/unauthorised. In the present case the Complainant
 went to withdraw some amount from ATM on 22.10.2018 and
 when the same was declined he immediately went to the
 Branch and got his Pass-book updated and he found that there
 was unauthorized withdrawal in his account of Rs.80,000/- by
 way of four ATM transactions and further there were two
 transfer entries of Rs.40,000/- and Rs.10,000/-. He gave
 complaint in writing to the OP on the same day (Exhibit CW-
 1/3) however despite receipt of such information OP did not
 keep CCTV footage of 22.10.2018 of ATM secured so as to
 ascertain who withdrew that amount from ATM.
14. As regards Transfer Entry of Rs.40,000/- and Rs.10,000/-
 on the same day i.e. 22.10.2018 are concerned, the same
 cannot be done without a signed Cheque or Debit Slip and for
 Debit Slip presence of account holder is required in the Bank's
 Branch with his Original Pass-book of his account. The
 Complainant has disputed these two transfer entries thereby
 contending that he did not go to the OP Bank's Branch on
 12.10.2018 if it was done through Debit Slip. Once these
 Transfer Entries were disputed then the onus shifted on OP to
 establish how these transfer entries were done in the account
 of the Complainant which OP failed to discharge. OP had
 related Cheque/Debit Slip/Voucher of 12.10.2018 in its
 custody but did not bother to check/examine how the two
 transfer entries were done in the account of the Complainant.
DISMISSED PAGE 5 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026
15. As regard the issue that the Complainant received message
 from the OP Bank on 12.10.2018 but he did not go through the
 same and got it deleted. Here also Bank has not contested the
 same by producing the contents of these messages before this
 Commission for its examination.
16. OP had primary responsibility to explain the 4 ATM
 transactions by way of CCTV footage and 2 transfer entries
 done in the account of the Complainant on 22.10.2018 but it
 chose not to put the same before the Commission in their
 defense and despite of service of Notice on them on 24.02.2022
 OP did not file Reply before this Commission. Hence there is
 no defense of the OP before this Commission and the
 complaint filed by the Complainant goes unrebutted and the
 Commission holds OP liable for deficiency in service.
17. For the reasons stated supra this Commission orders as
 follows:
⎯ OP to pay Rs.1,30,000/- to the Complainant with interest
 @6% p.a. from 12.10.2018 within 30 days of receipt of
 this Order.
⎯ OP to pay Rs.5000/- towards mental agony to the
 Complainant and Rs.5000/- towards the cost of the
 litigation.
If the above amount is not paid within 30 days from the date
 of the order then OP shall pay interest @8% p.a. from
 12.10.2018 on all the above amounts till the date of
 realization."
3. Aggrieved by the order passed by the District Commission, the
 Appellant/Opposite Party has preferred the present appeal submitting that the
 impugned order is contrary to the facts on record and violative of the

DISMISSED PAGE 6 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026

 principles of natural justice, because the Appellant was not afforded a
 reasonable opportunity of being heard. It is further submitted that the
 Respondent/Complainant had no locus standi to file the complaint, as he
 himself was negligent in the matter, having failed to report the unauthorized
 transactions to the bank within three working days of receiving
 communication in that regard, as mandated under the relevant RBI policy
 governing customer liability in cases of third-party fraudulent transactions,
 thereby disentitling himself from claiming zero liability. Pressing the
 aforesaid, the counsel for the Appellant submitted that there is no deficiency
 of service on the part of the Appellant and prayed for setting aside the
 impugned order passed by the District Commission.
4. The Respondent/Complainant, on the other hand, filed the reply to the present
 Appeal whereby, denied all the allegations of the Appellant and submitted that
 there is no error in the impugned order as the entire material available on
 record was properly scrutinized before passing the said order.
5. The parties were directed to file written arguments and the same have been
 filed by the Appellant and the Respondent, wherein the Appellant has relied
 upon the following judgments in support of its case:
a) Arjun singh v. Mohindra
kumar & ors., AIR 1964 SC 993
b) Brij Indar Singh v. Lala Kanshi Ram & Ors.
, AIR 1917 P.C. 156;
c) Manindra Land and Building Corporation Ltd. v. Bhutnath
 Banerjee & Ors.
, AIR 1964 SC 1336;
d) Mata Din v. A. Narayanan
, AIR 1970 SC 1953;
e) State of Bihar & Ors. v. Kameshwar Prasad Singh & Anr.
, AIR
 2000 SC 2306;
f) Madanlal v. Shyamlal
, AIR 2002 SC 100;
g) Davinder Pal Sehgal & Anr. v. M/s. Partap Steel Rolling Mills
 (P) Ltd. & Ors., AIR 2002 SC 451;
DISMISSED PAGE 7 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026
h) Ram Nath Sao alias
Ram Nath Sao & Ors. v. Gobardhan Sao &
 Ors.
, AIR 2002 SC 1201;
i) Kaushalya Devi v. Prem Chand & Anr., (2005) 10 SCC 127;
j) Srei International Finance Ltd., v. Fair growth Financial
 Services Ltd. & Anr., (2005) 13 SCC 95; and
k) Reena Sadh v. Anjana Enterprises
, AIR 2008 SC 2054.
6. The Respondent has also filed the written submissions whereby submitted that
 the Appellant bank is legally bound to safeguard the money of its customers
 and had the responsibility to explain the fraudulent transactions via CCTV
 footage.
7. We have perused the material available on record.
8. The primary question for consideration before us is whether the notice of the
 Complaint Case bearing no. 224/2019 was duly served upon the Appellant
 bank before the District Commission.
9. On perusal of the record, we find that the present case revolves around the
 unauthorised transactions amounting Rs. 1,30,000/- occurred from the bank
 account of the Respondent partially through ATM withdrawal and remaining
 through transfer from bank account and alleging the same, the Respondent has
 filed the consumer complaint bearing no. 224/2019 wherein, the notice of the
 complaint was duly served upon the Appellant/Opposite Party and received
 by one of the staff personnel of the Appellant on 24.02.2022. However, even
 after receiving the said notice, the Appellant failed to appear before the
 District Commission as well as failed to file the written statement therein,
 consequent to which, the District Commission was compelled to pass an ex-
 parte order on 01.11.2022, for wilful absence of Appellant/Opposite Party
 during the proceedings. Therefore, we find no merit in the submission of the
 Appellant that he was not given any opportunity of being heard before the
 District Commission.
DISMISSED PAGE 8 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026
10. The main questions for consideration before us are whether the District
 Commission has erred in establishing deficiency of service on the part of
 the Appellant/Opposite Party.
11. Upon perusal of the material available on record, we find that the Respondent,
 immediately after discovering the unauthorised transactions in the bank
 account, approached the Appellant Bank on 22.10.2018 and lodged a written
 complaint disputing the withdrawal of Rs.80,000/- through four ATM
 transactions and the subsequent transfer of Rs.40,000/- and Rs.10,000/- from
 his account. The Respondent also specifically requested the Appellant to
 verify the disputed transactions and furnish the CCTV footage of the
 concerned ATM. However, despite the complaint having been lodged within
 a reasonable time, the Appellant neither secured nor produced the CCTV
 footage before the District Commission or before this Commission. It is
 pertinent to note that the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI),
 vide Circular No. NPCI/2012-13/NFS/2737 dated 26.03.2013, mandates
 banks to facilitate the availability of CCTV recordings relating to disputed
 ATM transactions whenever sought by a customer.
12. We further find that the Appellant has failed to satisfactorily explain the
 manner in which the disputed transactions came to be affected as the record
 reveals that on 12.10.2018, four separate ATM withdrawals of Rs.20,000/-
 each, aggregating to Rs. 80,000/-, were processed from the bank account of
 the Respondent. However, the Appellant has neither disclosed the category of
 debit card issued to the Respondent nor explained how such withdrawals were
 permitted if the applicable daily withdrawal limit was lower than the amount
 actually withdrawn. Further, being the custodian of the electronic transaction
 logs, ATM journals, switch records and authentication details, the Appellant
 alone was in a position to establish that the transactions were duly
 authenticated and authorised. However, no such material has been filed by the
 Appellant. Furthermore, it is equally significant that the Respondent has

DISMISSED PAGE 9 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026

 submitted that his debit card was never lost or handed over to any third person.
 In such circumstances, the Appellant was expected to explain whether the
 transactions resulted from card cloning, skimming, compromise of the ATM
 terminal or any other technical vulnerability.
13. Additionally, the same negligence is evident in respect of the two account
 transfers of Rs. 40,000/- and Rs. 10,000/- made on the very same day to the
 bank account of person namely Mr. Sonu. The Respondent categorically
 denied having visited the branch or authorised any such transfers. It is noted
 that once the transactions were specifically disputed, the burden shifted upon
 the Appellant to produce the relevant debit slips, transfer vouchers,
 transaction authorisation details or any other contemporaneous record
 demonstrating that the transfer was authorised by the Respondent. Moreso,
 these documents were admittedly within the exclusive custody of the
 Appellant Bank, yet no effort was made either to verify or produce them
 before the District Commission. Likewise, despite receiving written
 complaints dated 22.10.2018 and 06.03.2019, the Appellant failed to conduct
 any meaningful investigation or furnish any reasoned response.
14. In view of the aforesaid discussion, we are of the considered opinion that the
 District Commission has rightly held the Appellant Bank guilty of deficiency
 in service as the Appellant failed to preserve and produce the CCTV footage
 of the disputed ATM transactions as well as failed to explain the processing
 of the unauthorised ATM withdrawals and amount transfers from bank
 account despite being in exclusive possession of the relevant electronic and
 documentary records, failed to substantiate that the transactions were duly
 authorised by the Respondent and failed to act upon the written complaints of
 the Respondent in accordance with the regulatory obligations governing
 unauthorised electronic banking transactions. These cumulative lapses
 completely undermine the defence set up by the Appellant and justify the
 findings returned by the District Commission.
DISMISSED PAGE 10 OF 11
 FA/176/2024 STATE BANK OF INDIA VS. MR. AMAR SINGH D.O.D.: 10.08.2026
15. Accordingly, we do not find any infirmity in the impugned order of the
 District Commission and agree with the reasons given by the District
 Commission. Consequently, we uphold the order dated 21.08.2023 passed
 by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (East), Govt. of
 NCT of Delhi, Convenient Shopping Centre, First Floor, Saini Enclave,
 Delhi - 110092.
16. Consequently, the present Appeal stands dismissed with no order as to costs.
17. Application(s) pending, if any, stand disposed of in terms of the aforesaid
 judgment.
18. The judgment be uploaded forthwith on the website of the commission for the
 perusal of the parties.
19. File be consigned to record room along with a copy of this Judgment.
(JUSTICE SANGITA DHINGRA SEHGAL)
 PRESIDENT

 (BIMLA KUMARI)
 MEMBER (FEMALE)

 Pronounced On:
10.08.2026
